- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., > -0.16 or 0.27), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or add lagged mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.27 or above), model underreacts to true price drop; increase downward forecast sensitivity or add 0.5–1.0% buffer below true low.
- Model consistently underestimates true price decline in early 30d horizon; apply 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment is negative.
- When sentiment is positive and price is falling, model often misreads trend; add 0.3–0.7% upward adjustment to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Forecast mean reversion is too aggressive; reduce mean reversion strength by 10–20% if sentiment is volatile or sentiment history shows mixed signals.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, model tends to overcorrect; apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias to forecast to avoid overbought correction.
